metadata.title: Infrastructure reliability incident investigation
metadata.artifact_scope_note: Evidence is aggregated query output (not raw log lines or metric samples); it contains no chat/communication records.

incident_description: Reliability incident investigation of a production environment. Evidence consists of Elasticsearch aggregation results over application and proxy logs, Kubernetes, cloud-provider and host system events, Prometheus Alertmanager alerts, change-management / CI-CD audit records and metric anomaly detection. No root cause, impact or trigger is stated; these must be established from the supplied artifacts. Environment context: Organization: Oakmark Go (ride-hailing); Platform: AWS eu-central-1 (zones eu-central-1a/eu-central-1b/eu-central-1c); network range 10.61.0.0/16; Kubernetes cluster oakmar-prod-eucent (EKS); Cluster add-ons: CoreDNS, ingress controller, Argo CD; services call external SaaS APIs; direct kubectl changes are recorded by the Kubernetes audit log with AUD- identifiers; Change management: production changes carry RFC- identifiers.
investigation_questions: Which service or infrastructure component did the incident originate in?
What change, deployment or automation run triggered the incident? Provide its change identifier.
Who (account or automation identity) executed the change that caused the incident?
What is the IP address of the cluster DNS service that the failing lookups were sent to?
Which external domains failed to resolve from inside the cluster?
During what hour did the first signs of the failure appear? Provide the earliest date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC format.

What is the root cause category of the incident: configuration change, software defect, hardware failure, cloud provider failure, capacity exhaustion, automation error, certificate expiry, or third-party dependency failure?
Which of the three CIA components is primarily affected: availability, integrity, or confidentiality?
According to the error volume statistics, what single service emitted the most errors? Is it the root cause or a downstream symptom?
Which change happened shortly before the incident began but did not cause it? Provide its identifier.
Which change restored normal service? Provide its change identifier.
